New 2026 PhD Cohort
We are pleased to welcome our newest cohort of Environmental Sciences and Society (ESS).
Whitney Barr
Whitney D. Barr holds a Master of Landscape Architecture from the University of Georgia and a B.A. in English from Spelman College. She is a food systems planner, designer, and ethnographic researcher with over a decade of experience across Georgia. Her research reimagines municipal food policy governance through mothers and children, positioning care as critical infrastructure and integrating ethnographic and geospatial/GeoAI methods in order to map how land use and regional food systems can better nourish resilient communities.
Tyler Tobias
Ty Tobias holds a B.S. in Environmental Studies with minors in Biology and Philosophy (Central Michigan University) and an M.S. in Wildlife Biology (Clemson University). Their experiences as a student and researcher situate their orientation toward critical, community-, and justice-oriented scholarship. Their research interests lie at the intersection of socio-ecological relationships, human-nature interactions, ecocultural service provisioning, sustenance and well-being, community and landscape ecology, and Black-Indigenous ecologies.
Chloe Loveland
Chloe Loveland holds a degree in Botany from Utah Valley University. Her undergraduate research examined how wildfires affect the mutualistic relationship between thatch ants and aphids, exploring ecological responses to environmental disturbance and climate change. At UVU’s Center for Social Impact, she served as a Social Impact Fellow, working on and contributing to applied research and community partnerships. At Emory, she will join Dr. Quave’s lab in the hopes of studying medicinal ethnobotany, investigating traditional plant knowledge and the phytochemical foundations of women’s health remedies.
Alexandra Juarez
Grethel “Alexandra” Juarez earned a Bachelor of Science in Biology and a minor in Biostatistics from Loyola University Chicago. Their undergraduate research experience and research assistantship at Michigan State University involved conducting ecological fieldwork and implementing computational pipelines. As a child of Central American immigrants, their research focuses on modeling the transmission and susceptibility of neglected tropical diseases in vulnerable populations globally and locally.
PhD - Environmental Sciences and Society (ESS)
By integrating environmental and social sciences, we empower our alumni to effectively confront the urgent environmental challenges of our time, fostering innovative solutions that promote sustainability and justice across diverse communities.
